# Current reconstruction status

**Full source, load-image equality and raw EXE equality achieved on 2026-10-06.**
`src/CERVII.PAS` compiles with unpatched TP6 to `build/game/CERVII.EXE`.
All 47,200 bytes match the original SHA-256, including the entire header,
44,016-byte load image and 787 ordered relocation entries. The executable is
generated from Pascal and standard compiler units without oracle linkage or
post-build patching. Reproduce with:

```powershell
.\scripts\build.ps1 -Tests -Supplemental -Verify
```

## Verified original

All 16 supplied game files are pinned in `assets.json`. They have not been modified.

| Property | Verified value |
| --- | --- |
| EXE size | 47,200 bytes |
| SHA-256 | `561ec217b7d4dcef9234843fbf6176c6178b0f72465ce4fb641d5403ab483eee` |
| MZ header | 3,184 bytes |
| Load image | 44,016 bytes |
| Relocations | 787 ordered entries |
| Entry | `0000:4626` |
| Stack | `0C13:3E80` (16,000 bytes) |
| Overlay/trailer | None |
| Minimum/maximum extra allocation | 1,340 / 42,300 paragraphs |

Direct calls at entry to System, Crt and Graph initialization, intact game/RTL
code and the relocation target segments strongly establish an unpacked Borland
real-mode MZ. There is no separate decompressor startup or reason to apply an
unpacker. Maximum allocation minus minimum is 40,960 paragraphs, consistent
with TP6's default 655,360-byte maximum heap. Stack size implies an explicit
16,000-byte stack. The recovered DS extent and `$M 16000,0,655360` naturally
reproduce both 1,340/42,300 allocation fields without header changes.
The lost directive spelling cannot be recovered uniquely.

## Compiler evidence

Canonical compiler: **Turbo Pascal 6.0, strong evidence**. TPC, standard units,
Graph, DOS runner and test emulator are pinned in `tools/toolchain.json`.
TP5.0, TP5.5, TP6.0 and TP7/BP7 real-mode TPC were tested.

| Compiler | Six shared RTL bodies, raw exact | 233-byte startup diagnostic |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TP5.0 | 6/6 | First difference at 43 |
| TP5.5 | 6/6 | First difference at 43 |
| TP6.0 | 6/6 | All 233 bytes match after specified address/call masks |
| TP7.0 | 6/6 | First difference at 11 |
| BP7.0 real-mode TPC | 6/6 | First difference at 11 |

The shared exact bodies total 166 bytes: GetDate, GetTime, GetIntVec, SetIntVec,
Sound and NoSound. These alone do not distinguish versions. System startup,
Graph InitGraph/CloseGraph offsets and recovered game code select TP6.
Twenty-four source routines additionally reproduce TP6's 286 code generation.
RangeCheck and StackCheck add 62 raw-exact RTL bytes in the declaration-aligned
probe, bringing the independently exact runtime-body total to 228 bytes.
Masked comparisons are diagnostics, never raw equality claims.
Detailed retained experiments are in `compiler-evidence.json`.

Recovered settings: `$G+`, `$S+`, `$R+`, software six-byte Real (`$N-`).
Game I/O checking is enabled around ordinary I/O and selectively disabled for
optional icon-file opens. Global `$I+` with local `$I-` is a source hypothesis.
`$A+` and the recovered declaration order reproduce all observed DS locations.
Unused directives and the exact original spelling/grouping of declarations
remain to be resolved.

## Canonical map and recovered source

`oracle/map.json` is regenerated from `scripts/map_binary.py`. Addresses are
load-image-relative and region ends are exclusive.

| Load range | Region | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `00000..04680` | Game, literals and bounds tables | Provisional complete extent |
| `04680..07AF0` | Borland Graph | Strong evidence |
| `07AF0..07B90` | Dos | Proven linked routines; includes alignment |
| `07B90..081B0` | Crt | Strong evidence |
| `081B0..09B90` | System | Strong evidence |
| `09B90..0ABF0` | Initialized data, 4,192 bytes | Byte-exact region match |
| `0ABF0..0C130` | Probable BSS/alignment, 5,440 bytes | Strong evidence |

There are 26 candidates: the keyboard interrupt, 24 frame prologues and the
compiler startup entry. The frame at `4635` belongs to main, not necessarily a
separate procedure. Candidate discovery does not prove every routine boundary;
indirect dispatch can leave gaps in recursive traversal.
`oracle/disassembly.txt` contains reached game instructions and linear RTL
disassembly; RTL inline data may decode as instructions and is not proof of code.

The procedural Pascal includes in `src/` contain twenty-four recovered routines totaling **16,730 bytes**:
keyboard interrupt, InitGraphics, InstallKeyboard, RestoreKeyboard,
CalibrateTiming, InitDirections, InitNotes, MusicTick, IconPixel, ShowIcon,
IconCursor, NextFreeColor, DrawDigit, DrawScores, RoundScreen, EditName,
PrintChoice, SpawnPlayer, BonusTick, ScorePanel, MovePlayer, PlayMatch, EditIcon and MainMenu.
All twenty-four match original routine
length and the explicitly limited compiler-shape diagnostic. A stricter check
also retains every global displacement byte, and all twenty-four pass it.
Near-call destination names are independently verified before their changing
relative operands are excluded. The full build resolves all far-call destinations.
**The small harness differs in raw bytes** because segments, CS pointers
and smart-linked runtime destinations differ. Global displacements now match.
`build/routines.json` retains both
raw differences and diagnostic results. Identifiers are provisional.
`src/DATA.INC` reproduces the 3,538-byte game constant region; TP6 supplies
586 bytes of Graph constants, 66 initialized System bytes and two final
alignment bytes. The entire **4,192-byte initialized region matches raw bytes**
in the DATA probe. All 29 named typed-constant locations match. Separate const
sections produce the observed word alignment naturally; no explicit padding
bytes are added. `build/initialized-data.json` records the proof.

`src/GLOBALS.INC` places 36 globals at the original DS offsets, including
runtime Input/Output at `234A/244A`. Relative stack start `DS+25A0`, stack
size 16,000 and minimum/maximum allocation fields match naturally.
Four unused word declarations have evidenced extents but provisional types.
The two final load-image alignment bytes overlap the beginning of BSS; this
does not imply that all uninitialized arrays start at zero.
The four-byte extent at DS:1824 is now modeled as one LongInt, TipecCount,
rather than two Integers: the match routine's single zero initialization
emits both consecutive stores naturally. Its name and unused purpose remain
provisional. This preserves every following DS offset. ShakerDelay is Word,
as established by the match loop's unsigned comparison and modulo division.

The flag array at DS:166A tracks occupied colors, as demonstrated by activation,
deactivation and color-change call sites and original-game tests. Its former
provisional name InactivePlayer has been replaced by ColorUsed; its helper
is NextFreeColor. Option bytes `DAF` and `DCD` are real SelfTipec and
UnlimitedTipec state, not padding; VertShaker is at `D83`.

The direction tables have bounds `0..180` but initialize only `0..179`;
they use the original decimal literal `3.141592765` and divide by 90, giving
two-degree steps. Do not substitute Pascal's Pi or change the divisor.
The keyboard array is `array[0..128] of Boolean`; installation deliberately
clears only 128 bytes. The interrupt emits a single `STI`, reproduced by
`asm sti end` because the original instruction enables nested interrupts and
ordinary Pascal has no corresponding statement. No copied code blob is used.
The note table has bounds `'a'..'h'` and signed Integer entries. InitNotes retains
an evidenced unused local word. Music advances every 14 calls and has a negative
phase tone ramp. Timing calibration squares a six-byte Real 20,000 times and
computes `6000 div elapsed - 21`, retaining its original division-by-zero risk.
SpawnPlayer resets death/place state, selects speed once, and retries direction
and elliptical placement when too close to earlier players. It preserves the
backward goto and all three pixel-history slots. EditName rolls an eight-character
field, ignores `0`, accepts `1..9`, prepends a space after backspace, and preserves
the previous value on Escape. Both source and original name scenarios confirm
the fixed-width result.
BonusTick reproduces all 384 bytes of instruction shape. Its timer is Word:
changing it to Integer introduces an extra compiler range check. The fixture
preserves the zero-to-65535 decrement, countdown, target retry and delay reset.

ScorePanel reproduces all 746 bytes of instruction shape and retains every DS
operand. It draws nested bands in ascending score order, splits ties across a
band, excludes inactive players, and ends at BestScore. When the winning
company size equals the final tie count, it enlarges the winner's 64x16 icon in
four frames and plays c/e/g/c tones. LastPlayer is assigned but unused, as in
the original. The source preserves the original assumptions about valid score
and winner state rather than adding bounds or termination guards.

MovePlayer reproduces all 3,263 bytes of instruction shape, every DS operand,
and its near calls to DrawDigit. Its two Real locals and three Word color
locals reproduce the original 20-byte stack frame. The three-point head moves
using the direction tables, with left/right wrap at 0/179 and rounding to
pixel coordinates. Points that do not change integer coordinates retain their
NextPixel values. Collision checks exclude overlaps with the previous head;
the last colliding point supplies the hit color. The routine draws before
handling death or company crossings. XCross permits linked-company crossings;
BonusType, SelfTipec and DeadTipec control collision awards, while placement
and VertShaker state are updated on death. UnlimitedTipec makes the selected
player white and suppresses collisions with nonwhite pixels; a final bonus
count of one restores the side colors. The original uninitialized HitColor
path when there is no collision is preserved, not normalized in production.

PlayMatch reproduces all 3,495 bytes of instruction shape, DS operands,
near-call bindings and its 1,450-byte stack frame. It counts company members,
loads typed 519-byte icon records with optional I/O checking, recolors icons
or draws name fallbacks, schedules three-point movement and music, processes
gun/shaker/time-bonus options, handles Escape and round waits, accumulates
company scores, and normalizes scores for the final panel. The original
wait accepts Space or Escape; Enter is not included. Two minimal assembly
calls discard ReadKey's return value while draining the buffer, reproducing
the original calls without extra locals or conditional instructions. They
invoke the unmodified Crt routine; no machine-code blob is embedded.
The spin-work Real literal is 1.23456789. The player scheduler retains its
backward jump across inactive slots, and the initial slowdown loop decrements
SpawnDelay on each spin-work iteration. These behaviors are preserved.

EditIcon reproduces all 1,982 bytes of instruction shape, DS operands,
near-call bindings and its 4,472-byte stack frame. Its three drawing helpers
are now nested procedures: the previously provisional unused argument was
TP6's hidden parent-frame link. Standalone helper fixtures retain an explicit
word modeling that link. TP6 omits nested public names from the MAP, so the
comparison locates each body through compiler source-line records for ICON.INC.
The extended prefix check additionally retains all helper calls and literals.

The editor reads five typed template records, strips spaces from the first
eight name characters, loads/recolors an optional ERB or initializes a blank
record, supports single-pixel drawing/erasing, cyclic shifts, continuous paint
and fill, then saves a 519-byte record on Escape. Home/End shift horizontally;
PageUp/PageDown shift vertically. Space cycles color/erase/off and Backspace
fills when painting is enabled. The original Down guard is Y < 63, although
only 16 rows are serialized. This is preserved, not corrected. Existing
unused record bytes survive GetImage; a newly initialized record leaves them
zero. Templates remain required, while the optional ERB read uses local I/O
checking control. Production code does not import oracle image bytes.

The first 17,704 game bytes, through MainMenu, match after excluding direct
far-call operands and relocated segment words. This includes all CS literals,
bounds tables, arithmetic constants, DS operands and near-call bytes in that
prefix. Its ordered relocation positions also match. `build/prefix.json`
keeps the raw differences and exact exclusions; this is not raw game-code equality.

## Verification and remaining work

The previously established canonical `scripts/build.ps1 -Tests` profile uses
DOSBox 0.74-3. On this computer that emulator is absent; its pins remain intact
and the default build fails with a missing-tool diagnostic. The separately
pinned `scripts/build.ps1 -Tests -Supplemental` uses the existing local
DOSBox-X (file version 2022.09.0). Its installation acquisition provenance is
unknown and is recorded as such. Both profiles use the same CPU/cycle/memory
settings; passing one profile does not establish timing equality to the other.

The supplemental profile passes hashes, compilation, fingerprints, mapping,
format analysis and 78 core, 50 match and 72 editor DOS source assertions.
Five score-panel assertions cover tied
score bands, inactive-player exclusion, preserved score state, company-gated
winner animation and a zero-score single-player band. Twenty-four movement
assertions cover steering wrap and simultaneous keys, translation and head
pixels, retained NextPixel values, collision/death and award caps, dead-player
and self-award options, placement, shaker start/extension, all three linked
company cases, unrelated companies, UnlimitedTipec and previous-head overlaps.
These execute reconstructed source; original-game round comparison remains
pending. The original BGI driver reports
ImageSize 518 and writes 516 image bytes for 64x16 pixels. These are emulator-side
ABI experiments and reconstructed-source fixtures. Original menu tests execute
the untouched EXE through DOS Exec, seed BIOS keys before launch and inspect
retained child data after exit. All 19 scenarios and 158 assertions pass.
They validate activation, names, color occupancy,
company links and mode/option changes. Complete gameplay validation remains
pending. See `BEHAVIOR.md` and `FORMATS.md`.

`probes/TESTMAT.PAS` executes the full recovered match routine in five isolated
scenarios: abort, missing icon, supplied BOG icon, optional features enabled,
and normal one-player completion. Each performs ten assertions on keyboard
restoration, termination, company sizes, scoring and cleanup state. A fixture
timer supplies Escape state and Space at the routine's actual waits; it does
not change production code. Inactive Place values are explicitly initialized
in the fixture because the score loop reads all six players. Option-enabled
execution does not establish exhaustive gun/shaker/time-bonus event coverage.
Reports are in `build/match/results.json`; original-match comparison is pending.
The option-enabled fixture exposed a timeout with its former fixed-delay
Escape signal. Abort fixtures now signal Escape only while the game keyboard
vector is installed, before repeated movement can exhaust all eligible bonus
targets. The original BonusTick retry still has no exit when no active living
player exists; production code is unchanged. This fixture avoids that path
rather than claiming to validate it.

`probes/TESTEDIT.PAS` runs twelve isolated editor cases with paced BIOS keys:
unchanged save, missing ERB, pixel paint/erase, four cyclic shifts, color fill,
erase fill, pen-off movement and movement below the serialized image. Each
checks keyboard-vector preservation, unchanged caller name, one typed record,
header, spare bytes and all 1,024 pixels after reload. Fixtures create their
own records in `build/editor`; supplied assets are unchanged. All 72 assertions
pass on DOSBox-X. Original-editor comparison remains pending.

The expanded fixture initially terminated because a new scoreboard test used
uninitialized test state. Its first runner check incorrectly accepted an empty
file. The fixture now initializes only its test prerequisites; production
behavior is unchanged. The runner requires a complete PASS line, rejects empty
and FAIL logs, flushes assertion checkpoints, and invalidates stale results
before each run. The corrected and expanded 78-assertion source fixture passes.
Build scripts remove each generated EXE/MAP before compiling and require fresh
outputs, so a failed historical compiler cannot leave an old successful binary
available to the comparison stages.

`scripts/build.ps1 -Verify` now succeeds with strict raw whole-EXE comparison.
It never lowers the closure criterion to masked equality. Build output never
links or patches oracle bytes. `build/comparison.json` retains the full report.

The complete menu/main source and smart-linked Graph/Dos/Crt/System selection
now converge naturally. Whole-file comparison exposed 12 differing bytes that
the masked probe could not detect: four Real conversion calls required Round
instead of Trunc, seven menu output calls required Write instead of WriteLn,
and the startup attribution required WriteLn instead of Write. Correcting the
Pascal statements made the full file exact; no compiler or binary patches were used.
The menu's 266-byte stack frame, ordinal Succ operations, team reassignment,
Welcome animation and start guards also match. The main attribution is retained
behind the original false condition.

Additional behavioral exploration remains optional: round/event interactions,
Welcome and editor interactions, and the canonical DOSBox profile. MUS/BAK
writer provenance is still unknown and must not be invented from residue alone.
Binary identity establishes the reconstructed executable; existing behavioral
fixtures cover only the scenarios described above.

missingno7-overkill-recon-docs-host-port.text:
# Native SDL3 platform phase

The DOS C baseline is complete. The native target compiles every `c/*.c` region and
replaces DOS hardware services with `host/` implementations. It now runs startup,
title, menus, level selection and gameplay through SDL3. The frozen ASM oracle and
DOS hybrid remain separate targets.

```powershell
python tools/host.py
.\build\host\OVERKILL_SDL3.exe
```

The first-run default is Tandy video with AdLib music and the original keyboard controls.
Later runs restore saved settings; explicit video or sound flags override their
respective saved choices using the original launcher policy.
`--video cga|ega|tandy` selects another original raster path. `--sound adlib|roland|off`
selects the music module; `off` leaves the original speaker effects setting intact.
Roland output uses Windows MIDI and needs a compatible synthesizer. The supplied
archive contains no Tandy music module. SDL gamepads supply the original calibration
and joystick policy rather than replacing the game's input decisions.

The executable, native core DLL, SDL3 DLL, source-generated initial image, original
assets and dependency licenses are placed together in `build/host`. Settings and
high scores go to `build/host/saves/HISCORE.DAT`; `--assets` and `--saves` override those
directories. The original assets are hash checked and remain unchanged.
Interactive runs append native stderr diagnostics to saves/OVERKILL.log (under
the selected save directory). Headless runs retain stderr for their test runner.

## State and oracle boundary

The native game executes C exclusively. It uses no CPU emulator, DOS executable
runner or ASM routine at runtime. `HOST_IMAGE.BIN` is inert, relocated initialization
and adjacent-data bytes derived from the source-built, hash-verified oracle. Offset
identities in original dispatch tables are routed to C functions and native services.
Unknown service identities fail explicitly.

`GAME_GEN.H`, `HOST_GEN.H` and sound-driver offset headers are generated from the
maintained ASM and its listings. One borrowed DS window and the same segment arena
retain the original records, links, CS variables, wrapped offsets and unchecked
sentinel accesses. No converted game records or synchronization copies are maintained.
EGA video planes are hardware state outside the conventional-memory arena.

Platform services provide archive/filesystem access, paragraph allocation and EMS,
CGA/Tandy/EGA raster operations, palette and text modes, keyboard events and character
reads, gamepad samples, and PIT timing. AdLib and Roland sequencers are C translations
of the optional source-built sound modules. Timestamped writes drive pinned Nuked OPL3,
speaker/PSG synthesis or MIDI output. Analog output levels and the compatible CP437
font are host presentation choices, not claims of identical historical hardware.

## Verification and deterministic runs

```powershell
python tools/hybrid.py
python tools/difftest.py
python tools/verify.py
python tests/host/input.py --no-build
python tests/host/rendering.py --no-build
python tests/host/video_services.py --no-build
python tests/host/graphics_decode.py
python tests/host/checkpoints.py --no-build
python tests/host/ui_flows.py --no-build
python tests/host/runtime.py
python tests/host/adlib_sequence.py
python tests/host/roland_sequence.py
```

Other `tests/host` suites cover memory aliases, movement, pools, terrain, combat, pods,
enemy paths, player/frame/weapon logic, file services and timer deadlines. Oracle
comparisons are bounded routine calls, not a boot of the original beyond gameplay
entry. CGA/Tandy pixel fixtures compare the arena against ASM; EGA plane fixtures use
independent plane expectations because the flat oracle emulator does not model EGA
hardware. Graphics decoding compares 50 shipped image assets across all three
adapters, including screen pages, panels and every level's sprite/block banks.
Both optional music sequencers compare state and ordered chip/MIDI writes.

Headless runs advance virtual time through the game's waits and input loops:

```powershell
.\build\host\OVERKILL_SDL3.exe --headless --milliseconds 48000 `
  --input-script controls.input --trace run.csv --screenshot frame.bmp
```

Input scripts contain sorted `milliseconds SDL_scancode pressed` rows, where pressed
is 0 or 1. Traces report service identities, selected state, quantized PCM and MIDI
hashes, and dropped audio events. The time budget stops the observation without
writing a save; normal quit and Alt+X use the game's shutdown/save policy.

Integration checks have exercised all six level selections and gameplay, all three
video adapters, pause/cheat-driven traversal of all six level-completion transitions,
AdLib and Roland startup, and Alt+X save/exit. The maintained runtime suite also
verifies Esc/Y returning through game over to the options menu, all six redefined
keys and SoundOption surviving save/reload, and one-sided launcher overrides.
Bounded native comparisons
cover all 24 actual checkpoint entries and segmented-boss placement, fire phases
and path wrapping. A ten-minute virtual gameplay soak completed without a runtime
failure and advanced to level two without F4 skips, with cheat flags enabled.
Live UI checks cover high-score name editing and keypad input, both quit answers,
boss-key restoration and cooperative timer delivery. Controller calibration uses
the shipped page and panel images with injected low/high/center gamepad samples;
the tests check its thresholds, overlay frames, release waits and Escape abort.
These checks do not establish exhaustive parity for every gameplay state. A dedicated
audio-backend regression gate remains to be added and validated. Full native parity
remains the completion bar.

The tested build uses Windows x86-64 MinGW GCC and the official SDL3 SDK pinned in
`metadata/sdl3.json`, downloaded only into ignored `build/deps`. A pkg-config compiler
branch exists for other hosts, but regenerating the oracle still needs the bundled
Windows DOS runners; an independent non-Windows build is not yet verified.

gerwout-dracula-adventure-engine-end-of-.text:
"""End-of-turn events — faithful port of DRACULA.EXE routine 0x269e.

The main loop calls this once after every command (EXE `0x030e: call 0x269e`),
then checks the death flag. It runs a linear fall-through of gated blocks:

  A. Dracula in your room (`room==dde & e70!=1`): land the counter-blow (`e74<0`
     → banish) or the combat counter escalates.
  B. Dracula patrol (`e76!=0 & dde!=24`): he steps one room 37→32→31→30→22→24;
     OR the room-24 confrontation (`room==24 & dde==24 & e76!=0`): defeat / escalate
     / death.
  C. Spider room (34): a proximity timer that warns then kills.
  D. Treasure win: carrying the schatkist into room 11 ends the game a winner.

Deaths set `eng.dead`; the win sets `eng.won` (the Engine ends the game on either).
Message indices are `world.messages` indices (the EXE `[0xe34]=K → messages[K-1]`
off-by-one is already applied). See docs/end-of-turn.md for the full disassembly.

Stub until the tests below it are green (TDD).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from .data.model import CARRIED
from . import verb_events

SCHATKIST = 13          # obj13, the schatkist ([0xc74]); carried == the treasure win
SPIN = 34               # obj34, the spider ([0xc9e]); its room drives the spider timer


def _cint(x: float) -> int:
    """QuickBASIC CINT — round to nearest, ties to even (banker's rounding), the
    semantics of the BASRUN fn 0x53 the computed-message formula ends with. Python's
    round() already implements round-half-to-even, so this is a thin, named wrapper."""
    return round(x)

# Dracula's one-step patrol path (EXE 0x2768): dde value -> (new dde, message index).
# He walks 37→32→31→30→22→24, one room per turn; the extra effects are handled inline.
_PATROL = {
    37: (32, 253),      # 0x27ff: also opens the iron gate (e44)
    32: (31, 252),      # 0x27e3
    31: (30, 251),      # 0x27c7
    30: (22, 250),      # 0x27ab
    22: (24, 249),      # 0x2783: also arms the bedroom door (e46) and resets e74=2
}


def run_end_of_turn(eng) -> None:
    """Port of EXE 0x269e — run once after each command; may set eng.dead/eng.won."""
    st = eng.state

    def flag(name):
        return st.get(name, 0)

    def pr(idx):
        if idx in eng.world.messages:
            eng.io.writeln(eng.world.message_text(idx))

    room = eng.room

    # --- Block A (0x26a4): you are standing in Dracula's room, not yet safe. -----
    if room == flag("dde") and flag("e70") != 1:
        if flag("e74") < 0:                       # counter-blow landed -> banish
            st["e70"] = 1
            st["dde"] = 255
            pr(149)
        elif flag("e74") == 5:                    # 0x26ea: computed Dracula-approach line
            # [0xe34] = CINT(RND*1 + 148.0) -> world.messages[[0xe34]-1] = messages[147]
            # or [148] ('Dracula komt langzaam dichterbij' / '...begint te lachen').
            # The DGROUP const 0x163a is MBF 148.0 — a message-index BASE, NOT 296 K
            # (the old temperature reading was a bias-128 decode error). NON-fatal.
            idx = _cint(148.0 + eng.rng.random())
            pr(idx - 1)
            st["e74"] = flag("e74") + 1           # 0x2742: escalate to phase 6
        elif flag("e74") == 6:                    # 0x2714: computed Dracula-attack -> DEATH
            # [0xe34] = CINT(RND*1 + 152.0) -> messages[151] or [152] (the neck-bite
            # collapse, the death climax). 0x163e is MBF 152.0. Sets [0xdf6]=-1 (death).
            idx = _cint(152.0 + eng.rng.random())
            pr(idx - 1)
            eng.dead = True
        else:
            # e74 in {0,1,2,3,4}: escalate one phase (2->3->4->5), no message.
            st["e74"] = flag("e74") + 1

    # --- Block B (0x2749): patrol OR the room-24 confrontation. -----------------
    if flag("e76") != 0 and flag("dde") != 24:
        # Patrol (0x2768): Dracula steps one room closer; print only if you see him.
        seen = room == flag("dde")
        step = _PATROL.get(flag("dde"))
        if step is not None:
            new_dde, msg = step
            came_from = flag("dde")
            st["dde"] = new_dde
            st["de0"] = came_from
            if came_from == 37:
                st["e44"] = 1                     # 0x2815: opens the iron gate
            if came_from == 22:
                st["e46"] = -1                    # 0x279f: arms the bedroom door
                st["e74"] = 2                     # 0x2799: (re)start combat at phase 2
            if seen:
                pr(msg)
    elif room == 24 and flag("dde") == 24 and flag("e76") != 0:
        # Room-24 confrontation (0x285e).
        if flag("e74") < 0:                       # decisive stake -> Dracula defeated
            st["dde"] = 257
            st["e76"] = 0
            verb_events.reveal_secret(eng)        # 0x4de7: defeat message + dust reveal
                                                  # of the room-31 secret word ("incoronium")
        elif flag("e74") == 3:
            pr(254)
            st["e74"] = 4
        elif flag("e74") == 4:
            pr(255)
            st["e74"] = 5                         # (0x4e21 object-scatter deferred)
        elif flag("e74") == 7:
            pr(256)
            eng.dead = True
        else:
            st["e74"] = flag("e74") + 1

    # --- Block C (0x28d2): the spider's room (34, or wherever the spider is). ----
    if room == 34 or room == eng.obj_loc.get(SPIN):
        if flag("e7a") > 3:
            pr(269)
            eng.dead = True
        elif flag("e7a") == 2:
            pr(270)
            st["e7a"] = 3
        else:
            st["e7a"] = flag("e7a") + 1

    # --- Block D (0x2929): carry the schatkist home (room 11) -> you win. --------
    if room == 11 and eng.obj_loc.get(SCHATKIST) == CARRIED:
        pr(281)
        eng.won = True                            # (0x2948 scoring loop deferred)

finito3-opencode-shadowofthebeast3-docs-.text:
# Memory reconstruction + decrunch results

All work local-only (personal RE use). Extracted binaries stay in
`extracted/` (gitignored); repo holds docs + own tooling.

## 1. Reconstruction recipe (tools/reconstruct_mem.py)

WHDLoad-equivalent linear loads from Disk.N images into a 1 MB image:

| # | source | dest | size | note |
|---|--------|------|------|------|
| 1 | Disk1[$A6800] | mem[$7C000] | $3000 | 2nd-stage loader (track 31 side 1) |
| 2 | Disk1[$8E338] (= game $4AB38 + $43800) | mem[$59F80] | $16F80 | then decrunch -> $5A000 |
| 3 | Disk1[$1800] + Disk1[$78000] | mem[$7F80] | $33000 + $1634C | then decrunch -> $8000 |
| 4 | mem[$7DE28] (embedded in loader) | decrunch -> mem[$40000] | - | 10 KB output |
| 5 | Disk2[0] | mem[$68000] | 512 | LoadDOS D1=0 D2=1 |
| 6 | Disk2[1024] | mem[$6FF90] | 4608 | LoadDOS D1=2 D2=9 |

The $43800 adjustment comes from the slave Load2: game offsets other than
$1800 are physicalized as `offset + $43800` on Disk.1.

## 2. Decrunch results (all checksums OK)

| output | size | content |
|--------|------|---------|
| mem[$5A000] | 136128 | tables (countdown patterns), then zeros; data tables |
| mem[$8000] | 375772 | main blob, 52x RTS markers; Ghidra base $8000: 17 functions ($81D2-$91F4), rest is data/gfx |
| mem[$40000] | 10244 | sparse (entropy 0.45), mostly zeros with small header |

LoadDOS magic verified: mem[$68004] = 0xB2FCA1FE matches the loader check.

## 3. Why direct decrunch of disk bytes fails

Proven by experiment: Disk.1[$4AB38] header is nonsense, Disk.1[$8E338]
decrunches fine. Pipeline order is disk -> Load2 sector processing ->
memory image -> ByteKiller -> data. `tools/bytekiller.py` is validated and
waits for memory-image input.

## 4. Engine scaffold (engine/, own code only)

TS + PixiJS, 50 Hz fixed step, dual-layer parallax placeholders, hero body
with jump/gravity, re-authored Level 1 structure from walkthrough prose
(platforms, crane, guns, spikes, hill, boss run). No original bytes.
Run: `cd engine && npm install && npm run dev`.

## 5. Level 1 findings (visual RE)

- Palette at to_8000+0x398 (32 colors): yellows 0FCC/0CA9/0A87/0975,
  test colors 000F/00F0/00FF/0F00/0F0F/0FF0/0FFF, forest greens/browns
  0120/0111/0960/0C00/0A52/0941/0730/0620, dark ramp, grays. Matches a
  forest level. Grayscale ramp at to_5A000+0 (fade table).
- Direct bitmap renders of data regions yield noise: graphics are stored
  as TILES + tilemap/placement streams, not linear bitmaps.
- Disk.2 file f20 (3000 B) shows sequential tile-placement records
  (incrementing IDs 153-155, 161-163, ... with separators 152/255/0).
- Small files fa2 (88 B), f22 (68 B), f30 (156 B) are sprite-sized with
  copper-ish headers; f28 (300 B) similar.
- Tool: tools/render_bp.py (bitplane -> PNG). Renders stay in
  extracted/renders/ (gitignored, personal use only).

## 6. Sprite rendering (visual RE proof)

Small files are Amiga sprites: 8-byte header + 16px-wide 2-plane bitmap
(4 bytes/row). Rendered with L1 palette (sprite colors 16+):
- fa2 (88B): striped red/brown pattern (platform edge / bar)
- f22 (68B): similar striped sprite
- f30 (156B): ornate door/panel shapes (pink/beige on black)
- f28 (300B): ornate vertical column (red/gold decor)
Tool: inline sprite() in analysis scripts; renders in extracted/renders/
(personal use only). Tile graphics (fa1 etc.) are likely compressed or
use different plane counts - next RE step.

## 7. Code vs data classification (Disk.2 files)

Raw code files (start with 68k `41 fa` LEA, contain RTS): `main` (3,4KB,
8 Ghidra funcs), `beast3p3.obj` (464B), `fa5` (76KB), `f24` (89KB),
`fc1` (190KB - biggest, likely main engine), plus fa4/f25/f27/f32
(RTS markers). These are loaded via LoadPsyFile and executed.
Sprite files (rendered OK as 16px 2-plane + 8B header): fa2, f22, f30,
f28 - ornamental decor, doors, columns.
Level stream: f20 (3000B sequential tile placements).
High-entropy unknowns (ByteKiller scan negative, no HUNK magic):
fa1, f01, f02, f29, f21, f23, ff0, fz0-3, beast3p1/2.obj - either
different compression/encryption or dense mixed code+data.

## 8. Emulator path (Maptapper-style memory dump)

Static tile guessing hit limits (copper changes colors per scanline; big
files use unknown packing). Per Maptapper docs, the reliable method is a
WinUAE save-state taken IN Level 1, then Tile Ripper on the memory dump
(ILBM 16x16 tiles are the most common Amiga format).
FS-UAE 3.2.35 portable runs headless-capable on Linux (verified binary
starts), but no Kickstart ROM is available in this environment, so the
dump must be produced where the game already runs (owner PC + WinUAE).
See docs/07-maptapper-guide.md.

## 9. Kickstart + WHDLoad setup (local)

- Kickstart 1.3 ROM: AmigaKickStart/ROMS/Kickstart 1.3.rom (MD5 82a21c1890cae844b3df741f2762d8d)
- WHDLoad USR package: downloaded from whdload.de, extracted to extracted/fsuae_hd/
  (WHDLoad, WHDLoad.VFS, WHDLoad.prefs, S/WHDLoad-Startup, DIC, RawDIC, Patcher, WArc)
- RTB relocation file: kick34005.A500.RTB (from skick346.lha)
- FS-UAE 3.2.35 portable runs on Linux (verified binary starts), but needs OpenGL
  (headless server has no GPU) -> use owner PC (WinUAE/FS-UAE) or GPU-equipped Linux.

## 10. Next steps (pixel-perfect map)

1. On owner PC: install WHDLoad, run Beast3 installer with original disks, play into
   Level 1, save state, load save state in Maptapper, rip ILBM tiles + map.
2. OR: use Unicorn Engine (M68K) to trace loader memory writes and reconstruct the
   memory image without GPU.
3. Parse entity/enemy/item positions from engine code + data files.
4. Extend engine scaffold with real palette, tile renderer, copper-based colors.

## 11. main.bin = MFM disk reader module (Disk.2, 3472 B, 8 Ghidra funcs)

Disassembly at base 0 shows low-level trackdisk routines (A5 = state,
A6 = $DFF000):
- FUN_826: filename matcher (12-byte compare loop, like LoadPsyFile .loop2)
- FUN_924: track/sector calc (mulu #$804, compare #$400)
- FUN_964: checksum (sum $200 words)
- FUN_97A: interrupt wait ($1E) + ack ($9C)
- FUN_9A4: CIA-B poll ($BFDD00 bit 4)
- FUN_9BE: MFM sync setup (writes $4489, fills $AAAB, disk DMA, checks
  $552AAAAA marker) - track sync + decode init
- FUN_B36: WORD-level MFM odd/even decode ($5555/$AAAB masks)
- FUN_B76: raster wait (VHPOSR $06 change detect)
So the game retains its own MFM path alongside WHDLoad linear loads.
fa5/f24/fc1 start with audio init (CLR AUDx, LEA $DFF0A0) = replay+engine
code files; fc1 (190KB) needs entry-point mapping (4B header).

## 12. RAM dump Level 1 -> pixel-perfect framebuffer (1lvl.dat)

Owner PC WinUAE RAM dump (1 MB chip RAM) while game runs in Level 1.
Tool `tools/copper_fb.py` parses the copperlist (default @0xD62):
- BPL1/2/3 pointers $071BB6/$071BDE/$071C06 (40 B apart = interleaved rows)
- 27 COLORxx MOVEs (bark browns 1-7, reds 17-19, sky blue-grays 21-31)
- Multi-band WAITs ($20/$26/$2C) = raster splits for parallax
Rendered 320x192x3 interleaved with copper palette = pixel-perfect Level 1
tree (trunk, branches, foliage) on transparent black. Renders in
extracted/renders/fb_L1_realpal.png (local, personal use only).
Second band ($07961A+) is a different buffer/layout (noise with same params).

## 13. Sprites from RAM dump (1lvl.dat)

Copperlist @0xD62 SPRxPTH/PTL: SPR0-1 off ($00000000), SPR2-5 at
$06A3CE/$06A42A/$06A486/$06A4E2, SPR6-7 at $06A316/$06A372 (each entry
92 B = 4 control + 88 bitmap = 16x22 2-plane). Rendered with L1 palette
banks 16/24: background mountain/cloud blobs (coherent shapes, not noise).
Hero sprite not yet isolated (may use attached pairs or other slots;
SPR0-1 off in this frame). Renders: extracted/renders/spr_all_b16_b24.png.

## 14. Tile format hunt (negative results narrow the search)

Tried on fa1 (25728 B) and to_8000 regions, all with L1 palette:
16x16x3/4/5 seq+int, 32x32x3/2, bit-reversed bytes, grayscale (geometry
check), autocorrelation strides 32-512 (flat), XOR/ROL/NIBBLE (no change).
All noise. Frequency analysis: fa1 top bytes 00/FF/80/01/10/08 (single-bit
values) = bitplane-like, NOT encrypted (encryption would flatten or shift
distribution, ROL/XOR preserve entropy which stayed 7.53).
Conclusion: tiles use non-standard layout (custom stride/interleave, RLE,
or code-mixed storage). f44 has only 15 RTS/93KB = mostly DATA with
repeating `00 89` pattern (634x) - candidate RLE/packed stream.
Next: Ghidra tile-blit routine in f44/fc1, or Maptapper save-state rip.

## 15. Save states (1s.uss/2s.uss) + scrolling proof

Owner PC WinUAE 6.0.3 ASF save states (states/1s.uss compressed, 2s.uss,
3s.wav audio). ASF chunks: CRAM/BRAM (512KB chip/fast, zlib w/ 8B header),
BPLX/SPR0-7/AUD/CIA (chip state). 1s.uss CRAM == 1lvl.dat at 96% (same
Level 1 moment); 2s.uss differs (other scroll position).
tools/copper_fb.py renders ANY state: 2s.uss @0xD5A gives same tree
scrolled left + second tree entering right = horizontal scrolling proven.
Stitch multiple scroll positions -> full Level 1 map (next step).
3s.wav = gameplay audio capture (MP3 gamerip exists online for reference).

## 16. Multi-state Level 1 screens (states/*.uss)

Owner saved 7 states across Level 1. copper_fb.py renders each:
- 1s/1lvl/2s: big tree, different scroll X (scrolling proven)
- 2a: black (transition/loading frame)
- 3a: three warrior figures (enemy encounter or hero frames)
- 4: crane puzzle (2 wheels + chain + hanging chains + 2 platforms)
- 5: platform gap (left/right mossy edges)
- 6: floating platforms (1 top-right, 2 bottom)
All 320x192x3 interleaved with copper palette. Renders in
extracted/renders/states/fb_*.png (personal use only).
Next: stitch by scroll into full L1 map; SPR/entities per state; audio.

## 17. SPR0/SPR1 ze stavu 3a (diagonalni fragment)

Copper SPR0=$02A69C, SPR1=$02A700 (oba 16x24 2-plane, 100 B spacing).
Render jednotlive (banky 16/20/24/28) i attached (16 barev 16-31):
diagonalni hnedo-cerveny pas s detaily = fragment (zbran? ruka? efekt?),
ne cela postava. Tri bojovnici z fb_3a jsou v BITPLANE framebufferu
(bobove vykreslene do playfieldu), ne HW sprity. Hrdina je pravdepodobne
bob nebo jiny SPR slot/par; k overeni pomuze hrac (viz fb_3a).
Renders: extracted/renders/hero*.png (lokalne).

## 18. Dual-layer framebuffer solved (3a.uss)

Odd planes ($071BB6/$071BDE/$071C06, 40B/row) = layer 1 (tree/warriors).
Even planes ($07961A/$079646/$079672, 44B/row = 352px) = layer 2
(forest canopy, floating island, ground). Copper switches bands via WAITs.
Renders: fb_3a.png (L1), pf2_3a_rb44.png (L2). Palette per band comes from
copper COLORxx MOVEs (static render uses base palette; copper gradients
refine per scanline).

## 19. Copper emulator + dual playfield render (tools/copper_render.py)

Minimal copper interpreter (MOVE/WAIT/SKIP/END) tracking BPLxPTH/PTL,
COLOR00-31, BPLCON0/1, BPL1MOD/2MOD per scanline band; renders 6-plane
dual playfield (PF1=odd planes colors 0-7, PF2=even colors 8-15).
State 3a: warriors render in correct browns (was pink with static pal),
top black correct. Lower bands need scroll/modulo refinement (BPLCON1
fine-scroll + per-band pointers) - next iteration.

# AUDIT — Project State, Correct vs Misleading Information

**Date:** 2026-06-18 · **Branch:** `claude/repo-audit-map-editor-rt0v5l`
(identical to `main` @ `2855885`)

Purpose: establish the **real** progress of this reverse-engineering bench,
separate **correct** information from **bad/misleading** information that has
been blocking completion, and record the decision to re-approach the map editor
as clean modern C. This document is the single rationale index for the cleanup
applied in this pass (quarantine, status consolidation, `CLAUDE.md` recreation).

---

## 1. Branch reconciliation

`main` and `claude/repo-audit-map-editor-rt0v5l` point at the **same commit**
(`2855885`); there is no divergent branch work to merge. History is 6 linear
commits — an early phased import (Phase 1 C source → Phase 2 disasm/tooling →
Phase 3 data) topped by "Add files via upload" snapshots. **Conclusion:** the
"audit including branches" reduces to auditing one tree; no cross-branch
conflicts exist.

---

## 2. What is CORRECT (keep and trust)

| Area | Evidence | Tier |
|------|----------|------|
| VICEROY core hand-ports | `viceroy_source/` ~47 functions with `@asm` offsets; `VERIFICATION_LEDGER.md`, `COMPLETION.md` mark tiers honestly | BYTE_VERIFIED |
| Trust discipline | `notes/TRUTH_HIERARCHY.md`, `notes/rulings/RULINGS.md` — C reconstruction ranked *low trust* on purpose; corrections logged, not silently edited | — |
| `.MP` format | `formats/MP_FORMAT.md` — header, tile bit layout, terrain table from NAMES.TXT `$TERRAIN`, auto-forest byte-verified at `func_006204`; only 3 honest `TODO_VERIFY` items | mostly verified |
| Tooling | `tools/disasm_mz.py`, `sigmatch.py` (self-test 17/17), `rtlink/`, `reconstitute.py`, `verify.py` (319/319 round-trip) — self-contained | PASS |
| MAPEDIT raw evidence | `code/MAPEDIT/disasm/*.asm` (212 files), `*.json` (functions/relocs/strings/classification), `MAPEDIT_ANALYSIS.md`, `FUNCTION_INVENTORY.md` | authoritative |
| Asset round-trip (PAL, MP) | byte-perfect via `extract/encode_pal.py`, `extract/encode_mp.py` | PASS |

The honest tier system already exists in the *detail* docs. The problem was
never the underlying RE — it was the **top-level summaries layered over it**.

---

## 3. What is MISLEADING / REDUNDANT (the actual blockers)

### 3.1 The map-editor "source" is ~0% semantic *(fixed this pass)*
`mapedit_source/src/` was ~6,460 lines of auto-generated control-flow
skeletons — every function `@status SKELETON (auto-traced control flow;
semantics TBD)`, bodies reduced to `if (ax != 0) {}` with registers/meaning
discarded (e.g. `legacy_autogen/src/load_image/load_image_015CA2_0172C7.c:25`).
Yet `mapedit_source/README.md` claimed *"hand-ported semantic detail on the
largest functions."* **That claim was false for MAPEDIT** and is the central
piece of bad information: it presents ~6,500 lines of unusable scaffolding as
progress.
**Action taken:** moved to `mapedit_source/legacy_autogen/` with a do-not-cite
disclaimer; rewrote `mapedit_source/README.md`; wrote `mapedit_source/REWRITE_PLAN.md`
for the clean modern-C re-approach.

### 3.2 `CLAUDE.md` was missing but cited 30+ times *(fixed this pass)*
The "prime directive + agent roster" and hard-rules authority was referenced in
`formats/MP_FORMAT.md`, `BUILD.md`, `notes/STATE.md` (drawn in its tree),
`notes/PROJECT_BOARD.md` (marked `[x]` done), and many `docs/*`,
`viceroy_source/docs/*`, `tools/*` — but **did not exist**. Every "per CLAUDE.md
hard rule" citation resolved to nothing.
**Action taken:** reconstructed `/CLAUDE.md` from the surviving rule text, each
rule carrying its citation.

### 3.3 Contradictory / stale status docs *(banners + consolidation this pass)*
`PROGRESS.md` states "Phase 2 IN PROGRESS", "100% of 1,241 functions in citable
C", and "OPENING/CLOSING not started" — contradicted by
`DISASM_COMPLETION_FINAL.md` (sprint complete; OPENING/CLOSING classified to
99%+). Three docs competed to be "the status": `PROGRESS.md`, `STATUS.md`,
`DISASM_COMPLETION.md` (+ its `_FINAL` twin).
**Action taken:** `STATUS.md` designated single source of truth; STALE banners
added to `PROGRESS.md`, `DISASM_COMPLETION.md`, `WEEK1_SUMMARY.md`,
`OVERLAY_PLAN.md`; a "1 of 26 weeks executed" caveat added to `SIX_MONTH_PLAN.md`.

### 3.4 Inflated headline metrics *(corrected wording this pass)*
"100% of functions in citable C" and "99.36% lines identified" conflate
*syntactically tagged/stubbed* with *semantically understood*. Reality: ~3.8%
byte-verified; the rest are skeletons/stubs with syntactic tags. The *detail*
docs (`COMPLETION.md`, `VERIFICATION_LEDGER.md`) are honest; only the headlines
inflated.

### 3.5 Dangling paths *(annotated this pass)*
`extracted/...`, `colonize_src_v3/`, `viceroy_overlay_full.asm`,
`function_index.json` are cited in `notes/TRUTH_HIERARCHY.md` and ~16 other
files. `extracted/` was deleted + git-ignored (commit `b0aa17b`); committed
decoded data lives in `data_extracted/`.
**Action taken:** added a single path-convention note in `/CLAUDE.md` and
`notes/TRUTH_HIERARCHY.md` clarifying `extracted/` is regenerable/uncommitted
rather than rewriting every in-doc path (mass path-edits across 17 files would
risk more harm than the dangling references themselves).

### 3.6 `col.zip` vs the "no verbatim binaries" policy *(kept, per decision)*
`col.zip` (5.1 MB uncompressed, 600 files) is a **verbatim** bundle of the
original game, including `VICEROY.EXE` (494,910 bytes) and `AMER2.MP`. This
contradicts `README.md`'s stated policy: *"No verbatim binaries (they live only
as `bin/*.b64`)."* It is also redundant with `bin/*.b64` + `reconstitute.py`.
**Decision (user):** keep `col.zip`; recorded here as a known policy exception.
The policy text in `README.md` should be read with this exception in mind.

---

## 4. Corrected metrics (use these, not the headlines)

| Component | Honest state |
|-----------|--------------|
| VICEROY.EXE functions | ~1,241 detected; **~47 BYTE_VERIFIED (~3.8%)**; remainder SKELETON/RECONSTRUCTED with `@asm` citations |
| VICEROY overlay | ~691 functions auto-detected (~28% of the 362 KB overlay); deep semantics ~a handful of functions |
| OPENING / CLOSING.EXE | classified ≥99% *lines* (syntactic tags); source = honest RAW stubs, ~13 sigmatch BYTE_VERIFIED helpers |
| MAPEDIT.EXE | 210 functions detected; **0 hand-decoded to clean C**; 5 sigmatch BYTE_VERIFIED shared helpers; clean rewrite planned (`mapedit_source/REWRITE_PLAN.md`) |
| Assets | PAL + MP round-trip byte-perfect; full 319-file SHA round-trip via `verify.py` PASS; image extraction deferred (regenerable) |
| "lines identified" | ~99% **syntactic** tags ≠ semantic understanding (~few %). Do not quote the 99% figure as completion. |

---

## 5. Map-editor re-approach (decision)

The auto-traced skeleton cannot be "finished" — there is nothing to build on.
The map editor is being re-approached as a **clean, modern-C reconstruction**,
hand-decoding the genuinely MAPEDIT-specific functions (`.MP` read/write, menu
dispatcher, tile-palette UI) from `code/MAPEDIT/disasm/`, grounded only in
verified facts (NAMES.TXT terrain table, `func_006204` auto-forest, the `.MP`
format, sigmatch'd shared helpers), with the same cite-or-TBD discipline as
`viceroy_source/`. Full design: `mapedit_source/REWRITE_PLAN.md`. **No clean C
is written yet** — the rewrite is planned and awaits go-ahead.

---

## 6. Recommended next steps (not done this pass)

1. Execute `mapedit_source/REWRITE_PLAN.md` step 1–2 (terrain + `.MP` I/O) and
   prove the `AMER2.MP` round-trip with `tools/verify.py`.
2. Resolve the 3 `MP_FORMAT.md` `TODO_VERIFY` items by tracing the `.MP` loader.
3. Optionally reconcile the `README.md` "no verbatim binaries" wording with the
   `col.zip` exception, or relocate `col.zip` out of the tree if the policy is
   to be enforced.

  - game C 1435/1435 · c2-asm 87/87 · av-delink 517/517 · crt 195/195;
  - initialized data 341/341; LE sizes all exact;
  - placement: code starts 2234/2234 exact; data placement 1538/1538 named
    exact, 58 statics via delink/anchor;
  - **strict whole-code-object: 0 differing bytes / 508368** with only
    loader fixups masked and every relative branch displacement visible.

The burn-down diagnostic toolkit was retired 2026-07-15 (see git history);
verification is `c2 rebuild` + the reccmp fork.  All figures above were
re-verified after the parser migration onto `reccmp.formats` (whole file
0 differing bytes / 1,304,734 incl. the regenerated debug trailer).

## 1. Header provenance, not data placement

Corroborate original header filenames / include graph and the 35 non-data
lib32 slots only if an external source artifact appears.  Do not sacrifice
exact BSS placement for an unsupported filename guess.

## 2. Oracle data reintroduction (eventually)

The Mac/Windows oracle data (windows func/global maps, crossbuild map,
flag-survey results) was removed with the diagnostic toolkit; copies exist
outside the repo and can be reintroduced if a use case appears.

## 3. Windows oracle: break the operand-order canonicalization residue

The dual-target campaign (2026-07-17) verifies each TU against
CAESAR2.EXE build A with MSVC 4.0 /Od (`c2 win-verify` in the tooling
repo).  Most non-exact functions fall to ordinary source-shape recovery;
what remains in the ground-down TUs is a single residue class.

**The class.**  For commutative operands (`a + b`, `a * b`) and
relational mirrors (`a < b` vs `b > a`), MSVC 4.0 /Od chooses which
operand to load first by consulting compiler-internal expression/
identifier-table state, not source order.  Watcom DOES follow source
order, so the spelling is pinned by the DOS bytes and cannot be used to
steer MSVC.  When MSVC's choice differs from build A's, one instruction
changes length (reg,mem vs mem,reg / shl vs add+lea) and every later
branch displacement shifts with it.

**Currently blocked sites** (each is ONE decision plus its ripple):

- `formulae.c`: random_event temple-weight sum (125 B — med*2 vs
  large*4 first), adjust_peace_criteria (31 B), adjust_culture_criteria
  (36 B), do_promotion (25 B), get_army_totals (1 B),
  get_temple_tip (2 B);
- `pump.c`: InsertNode `text_buf[p + i]` (2 B);
- `lib32.c`: totalXpercentX100 imul order (2 B).

**Levers proven NOT to move these sites** (all tested on
random_event/adjust_peace, 2026-07-17): operand spelling and relational
mirroring; parenthesization; bool-assign vs if/else statement form;
`x*2` vs `2*x` vs `x+x`; extra extern declarations (new-name pads DO
move a different subclass — do_promotion/proserity responded — but not
these); renaming upstream locals (30-name sweep); sharing an upstream
local's identifier; fold-neutral expression-count edits (`+ 1 + 0`).
One working observation: a mul node SHARED with an earlier expression
in the TU (random_event's `large*4` also appears in its event-0 sum)
sits on the losing side, suggesting a fresh-vs-stale node rule — but
the same sharing exists in build A's source, so the rule must depend on
table state that diverged further upstream, beyond anything reachable
from this TU's text.

**What is missing to break it: the actual rule.**  Reverse-engineer the
canonicalization from MSVC 4.0's compiler itself:

1. extract the C compiler pass (C1.EXE / C1XX or the combined CL) from
   the `localhost/msvc-4.00-wibo` toolchain image in the tooling repo;
2. locate the expression-tree construction for binary commutative ops
   and the relational emitter — find the comparison that picks the
   first-loaded operand (likely an id/pointer compare on hash-consed
   nodes, given the observed insensitivity to names and counts);
3. model node-id assignment well enough to predict the choice from a
   TU prefix; validate the model against the ~40 already-exact
   formulae/pump functions (they constrain it tightly);
4. then either (a) find legitimate source text whose node history
   produces build A's choices, or (b) prove the divergence is caused by
   genuinely different Windows-era upstream source and classify those
   sites as per-build differences with a guard.

Secondary attacks if the disassembly route stalls: fully characterize
the decision function empirically (differential fuzzing of minimal TUs
against the site outcome), or bring in a second Windows build
(build B) as another witness to separate compiler state from source.

**Supporting fact worth keeping:** MSVC 4.0 assigns frame slots by
identifier-table order, so build A also fixes each function's local-name
hash layout.  The cohort/slave functions were made byte-exact by
searching names against that layout (reconstruction commit `47cc5bb`);
those names are witnesses, not recovered truth.  The same search
technique (bulk rank probes + per-function slot readers driving
`c2.win_bytes`) applies to every remaining slot-noise function and is
reconstructable from the tooling repo's `scripts/wv_check.py` /
`scripts/wv_tu.py` plus git history around caesar2 `9bd87bbf`.

## Explicitly out of scope

- byte-exact Watcom debug section;
- original source file/path strings and file naming;
- inverse-compiler research.

# Bounded compatibility profiles

This is a bounded prototype, not a complete WordStar editor. The reference is the primary floppy WS.EXE whose SHA-256 is `535235e6a392d344948d065a5553798e6119b2a0c25ccbaca2221b6b4860904d`.

## State and ownership

The Rust core owns exact document carrier bytes, a zero-based cursor byte offset, insert mode, and declared formatting (margins, right justification, line spacing, document mode). It keeps the original bytes for byte-based modification detection; this does not claim to reproduce the DOS modified flag. UI and CLI adapters do not reinterpret command semantics. Cursor offsets cannot split a framed character or a CR/LF pair, or move into padding. No universal screen-column or Unicode-index equivalence is assumed.

Parsing partitions every input byte without rewriting it. It distinguishes hard/soft CR paired with ordinary/page-marked LF, 1B/9B framing, high-bit text/control values, soft spaces, tabs, padding candidates, and unresolved input. These are structural interpretations from the local investigation. Recognizing a structure does not establish its rendering or editing behavior.

The first padding token is the bounded editing profile's active end. The entire carrier, including material after that token, is retained. Text mutations reject post-EOF payload. Typing and Enter validate the selected physical line; Ctrl-B validates its selected paragraph. Other active content retains its bytes. Structural navigation and mode toggling do not require text to be editable. Inspection remains available.

## Enter: ws4-ascii-enter-v1

Two synthetic, redistributable JSON scenarios refer to hashed retained DOS evidence:

| Scenario | Reference observation | Compared result |
|---|---|---|
| enter-insert-on-alpha-beta | New document, Insert on, CTLNFL=FF: ALPHA / Enter / BETA / save | All 128 saved bytes via SHA-256; insert mode |
| enter-insert-off-next-line | ALPHA CRLF BETA, start at L01 C01, Insert off, CTLNFL=FF, Enter / save | Unchanged 128 saved bytes; insert mode; byte offset 7 derived from observed L02 C01 |

The insert-on scenario's empty initial carrier is a synthetic representation of a new document, not a captured DOS memory buffer. Final cursor and screen are not compared there. Replay uses semantic commands and restores declared initial state; it does not execute DOS menus, key events, or the original program. Source references are verified separately by `tools/verify-local-evidence.py` against an explicitly selected local investigation directory.

The expected carrier is constructed as ASCII `ALPHA`, `0D 0A`, ASCII `BETA`, and 117 `1A` bytes, then checked against the retained captures. Original software, screenshots, dictionaries, and decompiled code are not included.

## ASCII editing: ws4-ascii-edit-v1

Forty-six additional scenarios qualify typing and Enter in plain or formatted text, including three sequences combining these operations with Ctrl-B. Each compares the saved carrier, final cursor, Insert mode, and declared formatting. The profile requires explicit initial formatting: document mode, single spacing and margins 1/65. Right justification may be on or off for local typing and Enter; Ctrl-B retains its separate justification-off restriction. The reference setup has word wrap enabled and CTLNFL=FF.

`insert_ascii` represents typed printable ASCII and obeys Insert mode. With Insert off it replaces text cells, then inserts any remaining characters before an intact hard/soft CRLF or at EOF. A typed space marks the preceding nonspace byte; ordinary typing preserves existing markers except where overwritten. The selected physical line may contain ASCII with highbit markers and A0 soft spaces. Other lines may contain opaque data and remain exact.

The local typing branch applies to characters starting in columns 1 through 65. This tests the cursor rather than the resulting line length: insertion near the start can extend an already long line. Beyond-margin spaces and automatic wrapping are now implemented under the additional wrapping profile below. A later unsupported branch rejects the entire typed command atomically.

Enter with Insert on inserts a hard CRLF at the cursor, preserving any existing break. With Insert off it moves past the next hard/soft CRLF without changing bytes; on a final unterminated line it appends CRLF at that line's end, including when invoked from the middle. Selected-line controls, tabs, framed characters, page-marked breaks, malformed data, and dot-command lines are unsupported. Errors leave bytes, cursor and modes unchanged. [Exact rules, comparisons and reopen evidence](EDITING.md).

Token-boundary movement, document-start navigation, and insert-mode toggling support replay. Their use in the declared sequences is compared; arbitrary visual navigation is not qualified.

## Ctrl-N: ws4-hard-break-v1

Two retained DOS runs with the distributed `CTLNFL=FF` setting show Ctrl-N inserting an ordinary hard CRLF at the cursor, with Insert both on and off. The saved bytes match the two CLI and desktop comparison scenarios. The cursor staying before the new break is derived from the unchanged left gap-buffer pointer, not a post-command screen. [Evidence, restrictions and untested cases](HARD_BREAK.md) define this profile. The `CTLNFL=00` memory-modified branch is excluded.

## Ctrl-B: ws4-ascii-reformat-v1

Reformat scenarios require explicit initial formatting. The supported settings are document mode, single spacing, margins 1/65, and right justification off. Ctrl-B starts at document start or immediately after an ordinary hard CRLF; it rebuilds one paragraph and moves to the next hard paragraph or EOF. The current implementation handles printable ASCII, existing highbit markers, soft spaces and ordinary soft breaks. [The 27 comparisons and exact exclusions](CTRL_B.md) define the evidence boundary.

Formatting settings remain explicit in snapshots and can be compared by replay. Restoring state is a harness operation, not evidence that the original uses the same internal representation. Unsupported settings are retained, then rejected by affected mutations before changing state.

## Automatic wrapping: ws4-ascii-wrap-v1

Forty-four additional scenarios compare typing across the right margin with right justification off. An ordinary space beyond column 65 is accepted without marking its predecessor. A nonspace first normalizes the current physical-line prefix, preserving the existing cursor byte and suffix. If the cursor remains beyond the margin, a bounded scanner places soft CRLFs and relocates it before ordinary insert/overwrite takes place. This is a distinct operation from full-paragraph Ctrl-B.

The scanner includes the existing byte under the cursor, so a space, letter or EOF there can produce different wrapping. Long first words are retained without forced splitting. Cleanup can also reduce the column enough to avoid wrapping. Original before/after states qualify these rules in Insert on/off cases, with preserved adjacent physical lines, and in two sequences combining wrapping, Enter, overwrite and Ctrl-B. [Exact rules, source evidence and reopen comparisons](WRAPPING.md).

Nonspace typing beyond the margin with right justification on, hyphen wrapping and the existing unsupported document/formatting conditions return explicit errors. Every typed batch stages its mutations and commits once.

## Vertical navigation: ws4-vertical-navigation-v1

Seven scenarios compare Ctrl-E/Ctrl-X movement with retained DOS status and synthetic input identities. On ordinary one-cell physical lines, the current column is clamped to the destination's end. The clamped column is used by the next move; there is no retained preferred column. Empty lines, the first and last line, and one observed soft-break transition are included. The core moves without changing carrier bytes or Insert mode. The Windows adapter routes Ctrl-E/Ctrl-X and Up/Down to the same core commands. [Observed sequences and limits](NAVIGATION.md) record the evidence. Page-marked breaks, dot commands, and opaque selected lines are rejected until their navigation semantics are qualified.

## Line boundaries: ws4-horizontal-boundary-v1

Five synthetic scenarios compare Ctrl-Q S/D on the first, second and empty final physical lines. The cursor moves to the current line's first cell or the position after its last text cell without changing the carrier. [Measured cases and limits](LINE_BOUNDARIES.md) identify the retained DOS screens. The profile excludes opaque lines, dot commands, page-marked breaks and non-document mode.

## Quick jumps: ws4-quick-jump-v1

Three scenarios compare Ctrl-Q B/K movement to placed block marks and Ctrl-Q C movement to document end. They check cursor offsets, retained marks and unchanged carrier bytes against an isolated DOS run. [Evidence and limits](QUICK_JUMPS.md) also record the original's missing-marker message, whose full modal display is not yet reproduced.

## Word navigation: ws4-word-navigation-v1

Twenty-seven scenarios compare Ctrl-A/Ctrl-F movement with retained DOS status and unchanged synthetic carrier bytes. Word movement is line-local. The measured punctuation cases distinguish comma as a separator from an internal hyphen that stays in a word. Marked letters move as ordinary letters; measured marked punctuation and periods before spaces act as separators. Ctrl-F on a hard CRLF reaches the next line start, but Ctrl-F from the preceding word does not cross the break. The core owns cursor movement; Windows Ctrl-A/Ctrl-F select the commands. [Observed cases and limits](WORD_NAVIGATION.md) record source identities. Other punctuation, soft breaks, and opaque selected lines remain unqualified.

## Literal search: ws4-ascii-find-v1

Seventeen synthetic scenarios compare Ctrl-Q F and Ctrl-L with retained DOS status screens and unchanged synthetic carrier bytes. Forward search, overlapping repetition, case sensitivity, whole words, backward search, and failure cursor positions are covered at declared starting positions. [Observed rules and limits](FIND.md) define the profile. The core owns search state; the Windows adapter displays the WordStar prompt.

## One-character search: ws4-character-find-v1

Eleven synthetic scenarios compare Ctrl-Q G/H with retained DOS screens and unchanged carriers. They cover forward and backward movement, repeated search, hard CRLF, case sensitivity, and failed-search boundaries. [Observed cases and limits](CHARACTER_FIND.md) define the profile.

## Search and replace: ws4-ascii-replace-v1

Twelve synthetic scenarios compare Ctrl-Q A, Y/N answers, the `N`, `W`, and `U` options, Ctrl-L repetition, no-match behavior, and changes in word length against retained DOS screens and saved carriers. Replacement changes one occurrence per invocation and leaves the cursor at its start. The core owns the pending answer and keeps the carrier unchanged until `Y`. [Observed cases, DOS reopen check and limits](REPLACEMENT.md) define the bounded alphabetic ASCII profile. Other replacement options and UTF-8 replacement remain unqualified.

## Ctrl-G deletion: ws4-delete-character-v1

Five synthetic scenarios compare Ctrl-G with retained DOS screenshots and saved bytes. On an ordinary text cell it removes that byte and keeps the cursor position. On a hard CRLF it joins two short ordinary lines. At EOF it has no effect. One high-bit text cell and Insert-off deletion are included. Windows Ctrl-G routes to the core command. [Observed cases and limits](DELETION.md) record source identities and the DOS reopen check. Soft-break deletion remains unqualified.

## Backspace and Delete: ws4-backspace-delete-v1

Ten synthetic scenarios compare physical Backspace and Delete with retained DOS screenshots and saved bytes. Backspace removes the previous byte and moves the cursor back; Delete removes the byte under the cursor and leaves the cursor in place. Both can join an ordinary hard break. Document boundaries, Insert-off mode and high-bit text are included. The desktop routes both keys through the core; Delete shares Ctrl-G's deletion command. [Observations, source identities, DOS reopen check and limits](BACKSPACE_DELETE.md) define the scope.

## Block marks and copy: ws4-block-copy-v1

Eight synthetic scenarios compare Ctrl-K B, Ctrl-K K and Ctrl-K C against retained DOS screenshots and saved bytes. The marks define a half-open byte range. Copy inserts those bytes at the cursor, leaves the cursor in place and retains the selection for repeated copying. Copy before and inside the selection, an ordinary hard CRLF, and Insert-off mode are covered. Incomplete or empty blocks are rejected atomically. [Observed cases, source identities, DOS reopen check and limits](BLOCK_COPY.md) define the scope. Later editing while marked remains unqualified.

## Block display: ws4-block-display-v1

Three retained scenarios compare Ctrl-K H hiding and restoring a marked single-line block, with unchanged saved bytes, cursor and marks. A separate menu run records the initial `turn display on` wording and the change after toggling. The portable core owns visibility; the Windows screen uses it to draw the selection, marker and menu wording. [Exact observations and limits](BLOCK_DISPLAY.md) define this profile.

## Block move and delete: ws4-block-move-delete-v1

Twenty synthetic scenarios compare Ctrl-K V and Ctrl-K Y with retained DOS screens and saved files. On an ordinary ASCII physical line, move relocates the block and its marks to a cursor position before or after the source. Delete clears the marks and can span one ordinary hard CRLF; it requires the cursor at or after the end mark. An end mark exactly one active byte before EOF is rejected because the DOS original loses that final byte in the measured move and delete cases. [Observed cases, DOS reopen checks and unresolved behavior](BLOCK_MOVE_DELETE.md) define the boundary. Cross-line movement and deletion across multiple breaks remain unqualified.

## Block write: ws4-block-write-single-line-v1

One isolated DOS case writes the marked `BC` in `ABCDE` to a new 128-byte file with `1A` padding. OpenStar's core and desktop file tests match the output SHA-256 and preserve the unsaved source and marks. The original prompts before overwriting an existing target; OpenStar refuses to replace it. [Starting conditions, output identity and limits](BLOCK_WRITE.md) define this narrow profile.

## File insertion: ws4-file-insert-single-line-v1

Two isolated DOS cases insert `XY` from a synthetic 128-byte WordStar file into `ABCDE`, with and without block marks. The cursor stays before the inserted text, and marks at the observed end position remain. OpenStar's saved output matches the unmarked DOS result byte for byte; the DOS original reopens and resaves that result without changes. [Starting conditions, file identities, reopen evidence and limits](FILE_INSERT.md) define the supported single-line ASCII profile.

## Ctrl-Y and Ctrl-U: ws4-line-erasure-v1

Fourteen synthetic scenarios compare whole-line deletion and reuse of the deleted-line buffer with retained DOS runs. Ctrl-Y deletes an ordinary physical line, including its hard CRLF when present, and moves to the line start. Ctrl-U inserts a copy of the buffer at the current cursor, leaves the cursor and Insert mode unchanged, and keeps the buffer for later use. Ctrl-G does not fill or clear this buffer in the observed sequences. [Cases, source identities, interoperability check, and limits](ERASURE.md) define the scope. The core owns the buffer; CLI and desktop adapters select commands without reproducing its rules.

## Ctrl-Q Y: ws4-line-right-erasure-v1

Six retained scenarios compare deletion from the cursor through the current line's text, Ctrl-U restoration, a hard-break no-op that preserves the buffer, and high-bit word-end markers. The cursor and hard break remain. One OpenStar output was reopened and resaved in DOS WordStar without byte changes. [Exact cases and limits](LINE_RIGHT.md) define this bounded profile.

## Ctrl-Q Delete: ws4-line-left-erasure-v1

Eight retained scenarios compare deletion from the current line start up to the cursor, Ctrl-U restoration, a line-start no-op that preserves the buffer, hard-break preservation, and high-bit word-end markers. The cursor moves to line start. One OpenStar output was reopened and resaved in DOS WordStar without byte changes. [Exact cases and limits](LINE_LEFT.md) define this bounded profile.

## Ctrl-T word erasure: ws4-word-erasure-v1

Twenty-seven synthetic scenarios compare Ctrl-T and its shared Ctrl-U buffer with retained DOS runs. At a word, Ctrl-T removes text from the cursor to a measured boundary; at spaces it removes the space run. On an ordinary hard break it joins the lines and clears the buffer. At EOF it leaves the buffer alone. Punctuation and adjacent-space cases are qualified only where measured. [Exact observations, source identities, interoperability check, and limits](WORD_ERASURE.md) define the scope. The core owns all erasure state.

## Carrier serialization

Explicit insertion, deletion, Enter and Ctrl-B serialize active bytes with at least two 1A bytes, padded to a multiple of 128 bytes. The old one-byte minimum was corrected using DOS captures at active lengths 126, 127, 128 and 129: their saved sizes are 128, 256, 256 and 256 bytes. The two-byte rule is a reconstruction generalized from these captures, not proof of every original save path or record boundary.

Ctrl-B also normalizes padding when active text is unchanged: 127 spaces grow from a 128-byte to a 256-byte carrier, while a 512-byte carrier containing only ALPHA shrinks to 128 bytes. Inspection, navigation, mode toggling, empty typing, and Enter that only moves the cursor preserve the exact original carrier. Selected Rust outputs have been reopened and saved in the original; see the Ctrl-B and editing reports for the tested scope.

## CLI and resource limits

`openstar inspect FILE` reads at most 64 MiB and reports SHA-256, complete token counts, and a bounded preview. At most 64 tokens and 32 raw bytes per token are displayed; the full carrier is examined. The first padding candidate does not stop tokenization.

`openstar replay CASE.json [--output NEW_FILE]` accepts at most 1 MiB of scenario JSON and 10000 commands. Unknown fields, versions, commands, malformed identities, and malformed hex are rejected. Output is created only after the declared comparisons pass, using the operating system's create-new operation. Existing files are never overwritten. An output I/O failure may leave the newly created file incomplete and is reported as failure.

## Remaining first-milestone work

General Ctrl-B behavior, right-justified and hyphen-aware wrapping, vertical movement outside the declared profile, and full file-save semantics remain unfinished. Ctrl-K S now saves the current file and creates a `.BAK` in the bounded local-file flow; concurrent writes and crash recovery remain unverified. [Observed save sequence and open questions](SAVING.md). The Windows interactive prototype has a bounded 80x25 screen comparison, including three scroll positions through line 14; later automatic page numbering is unknown. CP437 glyph rendering outside the tested screen, Unicode, input-method composition, accessibility, undo/recovery, PDF, and printing are separate work. Passing these profiles does not establish those features or general compatibility.

# Unnatural Selection file formats

Reverse-engineered from the 1993 DOS release (files dated 1996-12-24, the
re-release build). All integers are little-endian. Status: **✅ decoded**,
**🟡 partly understood**, **❌ not yet decoded**.

## Folder layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `UNS.EXE`, `UNS_LAB.EXE`, `UNS_BAT.EXE`, `UNS_PLOT.EXE` | Launcher, lab, battle and story-movie programs |
| `DATA/*.BIN` | Resource containers (graphics, text) |
| `DATA/*.DSN` | Sound / voice containers |
| `DATA/*.PAL` | 256-colour palettes |
| `DATA/*.FNT` | Bitmap fonts |
| `DATA/BODY.DEF`, `DATA/LAB.DEF` | Default Body and Lab Variables |
| `ISLANDS/*.ILN` | Battle islands (same container format as `.BIN`) |
| `SAVE/*.LAB` | Textbook experiments and saved labs |
| `SAVE/*.BVA`, `SAVE/*.LVA` | Per-island Body / Lab Variables (369 / 32 bytes) |
| `A_SNDS/*.DSN` | Movie dialogue audio |

## Resource containers (`.BIN`, `.ILN`) ✅

```
header: N entries x 8 bytes, N = (offset field of entry 0) / 8
  u16 size        bytes of entry data (NOT counting a palette chunk)
  u16 group       animation/sequence group number (0 for most files)
  u16 offset_lo   entry start (palette chunk first, if any) modulo 65536
  u8  type        'R','N','T','F','A','B','M' (see below)
  u8  pal_flag    0 = none; otherwise a palette chunk precedes the data
```

Entries are stored back to back after the header. Empty slots have size 0.
Because `offset_lo` is only 16 bits, readers walk the entries sequentially and
re-sync to the nearest position congruent to `offset_lo`.

Palette chunk sizes by `pal_flag`: 1 → 768 bytes (colours 0-255),
3 → 576 bytes (192 colours, loaded at index **64**), 5 → 192, 7 → 285,
8 → 18 (🟡 load index for 5/7/8 not confirmed). Colour components are 6-bit
VGA values (0-63).

The lab UI uses palette indices 0-63 only (from `5X.PAL`); full-screen
pictures, island maps and Zoom-3 claymation close-ups swap in their own colours
at 64-255.

### Type 'R' – RLE image ✅
```
u16 width, u16 height, u8 key (transparent colour; 0xFF = opaque)
RLE stream: 0x89 n v  -> (n + 1) copies of v
            any other -> one literal pixel
u8 checksum (trailing)
```

### Type 'N' – raw image ✅
`u16 width, u16 height, width*height pixel bytes, u8 checksum`.
Creature sprites use index 0x54 (dark grey) or 0 as background.

### Type 'T' – text ✅
Bytes XOR `0x8A`; terminated by a raw `0x00`. After XOR, values below 0x20 are
punctuation shifted down by 0x20 (`0x00` space, `0x0C` comma, `0x0E` period,
`0x07` apostrophe, `0x1F` question mark …). `AL5.BIN` holds the intro-movie
subtitles.

### Types 'F' / 'A' – animation ❌
Zoom-3 creature animations (`CH`, `CM`, `DIE`, `ET`, `F1`, `FBM`, `KA`, `MD`,
`MT`, `RW`, `SR`.BIN). Each sequence begins with a 512-byte 'A' table and a
palette-flagged first frame; the following 'F' entries start with
`aa 00 5a 00` (170x90) and appear to be delta frames. Next step: decode the
delta scheme by diffing consecutive frames.

### Types 'B', 'M' (islands) 🟡
Each `.ILN` has: two 260x100 'R' images (terrain map + overlay), a 'T'
briefing text, a 'B' (369 bytes = body variables), an 'M' (probably the
terrain/food/creature map), and a palette-flagged 260x100 'R' image.
260x100 / 4 = 6500, the manual's island population cap.

## Known contents

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `AL1.BIN` | Lab console (#2, 320x200 + palette), Body/Lab Variables panels (#23, #71), View panel (#39), dialogs, menus, cursors (#0-1), type icons (#15-17), food-tube levels (#126-129) |
| `AL2.BIN` | Battle console (#0), aircraft, cargo panels, SatBeam panel |
| `AL3.BIN` | Lab button on/off sprites: modules (#0-7), FIGHT/MATE (#10-13), SNI count buttons (#38-55), INJECT (#56-57), WALLS/FOOD (#58-61), mutation dial (#62-65), food flow (#66-73), zoom panel (#79) |
| `AL4.BIN` | Title screen, Maxis logo, desktop (Top Secret / Independent Research), dialogs |
| `AL5.BIN` | Movie subtitle text |
| `BACK.BIN` | Zoom-2 floor backgrounds (#0-11, 170x90) and Zoom-3 close-up portraits (palette-flagged entries, e.g. #12-16) |
| `ZIPS/HULKS/SLUGS/BEASTS/TANKS.BIN` | Zoom-2 creature sprites (~10x6, many headings/poses) |
| `SNI.BIN` | 85x45 injection animation (🟡 palette source unknown) |
| `S01…S25.BIN` + `.DSN` | Story-movie stills and their audio |
| `ISLTILES.BIN` | 🟡 island tile table, different format |

## Fonts (`.FNT`) ✅
`u8 glyph_width, u8 glyph_height`, then 90 glyphs for ASCII 32-121, one byte
per row, MSB = leftmost pixel.

## Default variables 🟡

`LAB.DEF` (32 bytes), best current reading:

| Offset | Bytes | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 4 | % chance to mutate for dial 0-3: `0 10 25 60` |
| 4 | 4 | Amount of mutation % for dial 0-3: `0 5 15 45` |
| 8 | 9 | Mutable attributes (1 = yes) |
| 17 | 2 | Dominant encounter trait and ? |
| 19 | 1 | Nutritional value (80) |
| 20 | 3 | Virus occurrence % X/Y/Z (10 10 10) |
| 23 | 3 | Virus results % (80 100 100) |
| 26 | 6 | Resupply intervals u16 for flow 1-3 (240 120 60) |

`BODY.DEF` (369 bytes) has per-body-type entries for Friendly and Enemy
creatures; not yet mapped. The `.LAB` saves embed a copy at offset 0x5B
followed by a lab-variables block.

## Lab saves (`.LAB`) 🟡
Offset 0x14: experiment name (space padded). 0x5B: body variables (369 bytes),
then lab variables (32). Later: wall/food grids, creature records, and a
170x90 grid of u16 cells (`0x8001` = empty floor, `0x8008` food, …). Decoding
these would let the remake load the Textbook Experiments (31 files in `SAVE/`) directly.

## Sound (`.DSN`) ❌
Starts with a table of (offset, length) pairs; the payload looks like 4-bit
ADPCM (credits list an in-house "audio compression" driver). Not yet decoded.
